title: I Took the Community-Loom Warp Booking to the Weaver Who Left My Warp on the Beam

parts.text: I sat at loom three at 1:07 p.m. and weaver Corin was already winding over my numbered warp. The slate said: ONE LOOM. THREE HOURS. WARP STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty-seven, guild member, holding a draft that listed our sett. Corin shrugged. "Weavers are the beam." I photographed the slate, the booking, and his bobbin on my warp. Then I asked for the loom log. At 1:15 the studio pinged why Corin's name was on my beam. I kept my voice studio-soft and let the timestamp talk. A slate is only a slate until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Corin's bobbin on my warp during our booking.

social.video_title: He wound over my numbered warp on my beam — Part 1/2
social.description: Community loom, a weaver on my warp, a three-hour clock he posted. I logged the wind. Would you have asked for the loom log?

parts.text: Corin called it a sample until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the slate, and the bobbin still. The warp went back to my lease sticks. Corin ran his own three hours and told the next weaver atmosphere was always about tension. Tension is a word weavers use when a booking exists. Loom policy now has a second line: WEAVERS ARE NOT THE BEAM. I keep our draft on a labeled clip. Corin brown-bags his jokes. The loom finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Weavers are not the beam — Part 2/2
social.description: Loom log, numbered warp, and a second line on the slate. Was a sample ever my beam?
